use_restriction: None of these records is an approved production EvidenceRecord. Numeric associations, distributions, model performance, and measurement errors must not be converted into interview scoring thresholds.

records.construct_name: Composite visual interview cues and interviewer judgment
records.measurement_name: Composite of physical attractiveness, smiling, gaze, hand movement, and body orientation
records.measurement_definition: Five manually rated visual cues combined into an overall visual cue index.
records.extraction_location: Abstract and Results, printed pages 986 and 991; Table 2
records.extraction_note: Correlation between the visual-cue composite and interviewers' judgments; p < .05.
records.author_interpretation: Visual cues can affect interviewers' judgments, with personal reactions proposed as a mediating explanation.
facefit_limitations: Composite includes appearance and hand movement outside Face-Fit scope
No head axes, shoulder line, baseline, or percentile

records.construct_name: Composite visual interview cues and job performance
records.measurement_name: Composite of physical attractiveness, smiling, gaze, hand movement, and body orientation
records.measurement_definition: Five manually rated visual cues combined into an overall visual cue index.
records.context_scope: Videotaped employment interviews and supervisory job-performance ratings
records.extraction_location: Abstract and Results, printed pages 986 and 991; Table 2
records.extraction_note: Correlation with job performance; p < .07, so the paper did not report conventional p < .05 significance.
records.author_interpretation: The result was presented as tentative evidence that visual cues may relate to later performance.
facefit_limitations: Composite is not a Face-Fit metric

records.construct_name: Applicant vertical visual motion and hirability variables
records.measurement_definition: Average vertical component of optical flow from the applicant's quasi-frontal upper-body video.
records.extraction_note: The table reports .330 for an applicant vertical-flow average association; exact dependent-column interpretation must be rechecked during expert review before registry ingestion.
records.author_interpretation: Applicant visual activity contributed information for computational hirability inference.
facefit_limitations: Optical flow includes more than shoulder-center motion
Absolute video activity, not session-relative shoulder velocity
Single job type and Swiss student-heavy sample

records.construct_name: Applicant motion-history visual activity and hirability variables
records.measurement_definition: Average weighted motion energy image statistic from applicant upper-body video.
records.extraction_note: The table reports .280 for applicant WMEI average; the broad motion-image construct is not a shoulder-specific measure.
records.author_interpretation: Motion-history features showed associations with parts of the hirability-rating set.

records.measurement_definition: Cross-validated prediction using the paper's combined nonverbal feature set.
records.extraction_note: Best reported ridge result for hiring-decision prediction using combined features.
records.author_interpretation: Automatically extracted nonverbal behavior provided predictive information for hirability ratings.
facefit_limitations: Multimodal model performance is not a behavior effect size
Cross-validation design differs from operational use

records.construct_name: Automated prediction of interview overall performance
records.measurement_definition: Correlation between model predictions and judges' overall/hiring ratings from aggregate facial, prosodic, and language features.
records.extraction_location: Section 6 and Table 5, printed page 200 (PDF page 10)
records.extraction_note: Paper reports correlations above .62 for overall and hiring outcomes; the exact value varies by model/target.
records.author_interpretation: Aggregate multimodal features can predict several interview ratings.
facefit_limitations: Model combines language, prosody, smile, head gesture, and facial points
Aggregate model metric is not a behavioral threshold

records.measurement_definition: Model discrimination for recommend-hiring judgments using multimodal aggregate features.
records.extraction_note: Recommend-hiring AUC reported as .80.
records.author_interpretation: Multimodal behavior supported useful discrimination of judges' ratings.
facefit_limitations: Classification performance does not define acceptable head motion
Rating target may contain rater bias
No threshold transferable to a new population

records.construct_name: Reliability of human hiring recommendation ratings
records.measurement_definition: Agreement among five experienced raters using a seven-point hiring-recommendation scale.
records.extraction_note: Hiring ICC=.79; this validates rater consistency, not any physical behavior.
records.author_interpretation: Experienced raters achieved substantial reliability on the hiring target used for automated modeling.
facefit_limitations: Hiring labels may encode human bias

records.construct_name: Broad head movement and interview performance
records.measurement_definition: Corrected association between the broad nonverbal category 'head movement' and interview-performance ratings.
records.population_scope: Subset of 63 studies; overall meta-analysis N=4,868
records.context_scope: Employment interviews across structures, modalities, durations, and real/mock settings
records.extraction_location: Article Summary and Results, printed pages 142-147; detailed cue results table in article
records.extraction_note: Head movement was among the strongest reported nonverbal associations (rho=.43).
records.author_interpretation: Head movement is meaningfully associated with interview ratings, while design and gender moderators caution against simple universal interpretations.
facefit_limitations: Direction and amount may differ across included studies
No interval statistic or operational cut point

records.measurement_definition: Corrected association between coded eye contact and interview-performance ratings.
records.population_scope: Subset of 63 studies; overall meta-analysis N=4,868
records.extraction_location: Article Summary and Results, printed pages 142-147
records.extraction_note: Eye contact rho=.45. Face-Fit currently does not implement gaze; head pose can only be considered an imperfect proxy.
records.author_interpretation: Eye contact was strongly associated with interview ratings.
facefit_limitations: Eye gaze is not head pose
Head orientation cannot establish visual fixation

records.measurement_definition: Review of eight structured-interview research topics with meta-analytic review when possible.
records.extraction_location: Abstract and full article, printed pages 241-293
records.extraction_note: No yaw, pitch, roll, shoulder, movement-percentile, or webcam kinematic threshold is reported.
records.author_interpretation: Interview structure improves standardization but many research questions remain.
facefit_limitations: Review is not a kinematic measurement study
Does not validate automated nonverbal scoring

records.measurement_definition: Review organizing 278 studies into social, cognitive, individual-difference, measurement, and outcome factors.
records.extraction_note: The count describes reviewed studies, not an effect or threshold.
records.author_interpretation: Interview outcomes arise from multiple social, cognitive, measurement, and contextual factors.
facefit_limitations: Broad review predates modern webcam pose estimation

records.measurement_definition: Correlation between visual-model predictions derived from Kinect body/head movement and holistic human ratings.
records.extraction_note: Random-forest visual-only correlation=.202; SVM value=.132.
records.author_interpretation: Visual features alone contributed less than speech or multimodal combinations in this small corpus.

records.measurement_definition: Correlation between combined lexical, speech, and visual model predictions and holistic human ratings.
records.extraction_note: Best reported multimodal correlation=.447 for the SVM configuration; random forest=.416.
records.author_interpretation: Combining modalities improved prediction over visual-only modeling.
facefit_limitations: Does not isolate head or shoulders

records.measurement_name: Ensemble prediction correlation for overall performance
records.measurement_definition: Leave-one-speaker-out correlation between multimodal ensemble-tree predictions and averaged expert overall-performance ratings.
records.extraction_note: Overall multimodal ensemble correlation=.745.
records.author_interpretation: Multimodal ensembles approximated expert performance ratings better than single modalities.
facefit_limitations: Overall model mixes acoustic, gaze, face, head, gestures, and Kinect body features
Predictive performance is not a threshold

records.measurement_definition: The paper classified audience-looking intervals using OKAO gaze or CLNF head orientation and divided looking time by presentation length.
records.extraction_location: Section 4, Visual Behavior Assessment, printed page 46
records.extraction_note: Angle intervals were calculated from eye-contact annotations, but the numeric angle boundaries are not reported.
records.author_interpretation: Head orientation can contribute to an audience-looking classifier in a calibrated public-speaking setup.
facefit_limitations: Head pose is only a gaze proxy
Virtual audience geometry differs from webcam interview

records.measurement_name: Distinct practices identified in semi-structured expert interviews
records.measurement_definition: Qualitative coding of public-speaking experts' views about nonverbal practices and multimodal coaching.
records.population_scope: Public-speaking experts; expert count NOT_REPORTED in accessible abstract
records.extraction_note: The count is qualitative coverage, not a validated behavioral scale or threshold.
records.author_interpretation: The work sought grounding because the Presentation Trainer lacked a valid assessment model for nonverbal presentation behavior.
facefit_limitations: Sensor details unavailable in accessible abstract

records.construct_name: Frequency and heterogeneity of observed public-speaking indicators
records.measurement_name: Indicator frequency in studies using non-validated instruments
records.measurement_definition: Scoping-review count of studies that included posture, head movement, or eye contact as evaluator-observed indicators.
records.population_scope: 35 adult public-speaking studies; indicator-frequency denominator is 26 studies using non-validated instruments
records.extraction_location: Results, Figure 1 and Table 3; Discussion, Nonverbal Behaviors subsection
records.extraction_note: Frequencies describe how often constructs were included in instruments, not the magnitude or effect of participant behavior.
records.author_interpretation: Public-speaking instruments repeatedly include eye contact, gestures, posture, and facial expression, but terminology and measurement are heterogeneous and many instruments were author-developed rather than validated.
facefit_limitations: Human observation studies only; technological assessment was excluded
No camera, angle, baseline, percentile, or threshold

records.measurement_definition: Organized survey of head-pose estimation approaches and their advantages and disadvantages.
records.extraction_note: Survey size only; no universal accuracy or behavior threshold.
records.author_interpretation: Head-pose estimation presents substantial identity, appearance, and evaluation challenges, with method-specific tradeoffs.

records.measurement_name: Hopenet alpha=2 axis and overall MAE on AFLW2000
records.measurement_definition: Mean absolute error between predicted and benchmark yaw, pitch, and roll angles.
records.extraction_note: Hopenet alpha=2 result.
records.author_interpretation: Joint binned classification and regression can estimate fine-grained Euler angles without keypoints.
facefit_limitations: Benchmark MAE is not interview behavior
Absolute benchmark pose differs from session-relative p95

records.measurement_name: Hopenet alpha=1 axis and overall MAE on BIWI
records.measurement_definition: Mean absolute error between predicted and benchmark yaw, pitch, and roll angles.
records.extraction_note: Hopenet alpha=1 result.
records.author_interpretation: The approach generalized to BIWI with dataset-specific error.

records.measurement_definition: Mean absolute error for yaw, pitch, roll, and their mean.
records.extraction_note: FSA-Caps-Fusion row.
records.author_interpretation: Fine-grained structure aggregation improved compact head-pose estimation.
facefit_limitations: MAE does not define acceptable behavior
Absolute image angles rather than session-relative interval statistics

records.measurement_definition: Toolkit estimates head pose together with facial landmarks, gaze, and action units from images and videos.
records.extraction_location: Abstract and system overview, printed pages 59-61
records.extraction_note: Independent validation is required for numeric error; toolkit capability alone is not evidence of Face-Fit accuracy.
records.author_interpretation: OpenFace 2.0 provides an accessible real-time facial-behavior analysis pipeline.

records.measurement_definition: Average signed difference between MediaPipe yaw and optoelectronic reference over controlled head movements.
records.extraction_note: Reported SD=10.65 degrees.
records.author_interpretation: MediaPipe accuracy reduced for large rotations; landmark errors contributed to failures.
facefit_limitations: Mean signed error, not behavior distribution
Face-Fit uses relative PnP and 5 FPS
Participant count not reported in extracted text

records.measurement_definition: Average signed difference between MediaPipe pitch and optoelectronic reference over controlled head movements.
records.extraction_note: Reported SD=10.22 degrees.
records.author_interpretation: MediaPipe showed reduced accuracy at large flexion/extension angles.
facefit_limitations: Measurement error is not acceptable interview pitch
Mean bias differs from absolute p95

records.measurement_definition: Average signed difference between MediaPipe roll and optoelectronic reference over controlled head movements.
records.extraction_note: Reported SD=2.44 degrees.
records.author_interpretation: Roll errors remained smaller than large-angle yaw and pitch errors in this controlled task.
facefit_limitations: Does not establish good or bad roll
Mean error cannot become p95 behavior threshold

records.measurement_definition: Bottom-up 2D body-part localization and person association in images.
records.extraction_note: Benchmark superiority does not validate Face-Fit shoulder tilt or behavior scoring.
records.author_interpretation: Part Affinity Fields support accurate, efficient multi-person 2D pose association.

records.measurement_name: Distribution of joint-position MAE across trials
records.measurement_definition: Mean absolute error of OpenPose-derived 3D joint positions against marker-based motion capture.
records.population_scope: Two healthy male participants across walking, jump, and throw tasks
records.extraction_location: Abstract and Discussion, article pages 1 and 8; Figure 3
records.extraction_note: Authors link >40 mm cases primarily to obvious 2D tracking failures.
records.author_interpretation: With correction of erroneous tracking, the multi-camera system may achieve joint-position accuracy of 30 mm or less for human movement research.

records.construct_name: Single-view 2D markerless occlusion and view effects
records.measurement_definition: Repeated-measures Bland-Altman comparison of OpenPose 2D joint angles with reprojected marker-based motion capture.
records.extraction_location: Abstract; Methods Sections 2.2-2.4; Discussion, article pages 1, 5-7, and 13-14
records.extraction_note: Occluded-side sagittal hip/knee agreement was worse; no left-right shoulder-line tilt outcome was tested.
records.author_interpretation: View and occlusion materially affect single-view 2D markerless kinematics, and some frontal-plane outputs are not ready for practical use.
facefit_limitations: Shoulder locations used in processing but shoulder tilt not validated

records.measurement_name: OpenPose shoulder-flexion RMSE by camera view
records.measurement_definition: RMSE of the angle between shoulder-to-elbow and mid-hip-to-neck vectors against Vicon.
records.context_scope: Single-view 2D OpenPose validation at four camera angles
records.extraction_note: Corresponding shoulder biases were -26.07, -16.25, -19.24, and -18.00 degrees.
records.author_interpretation: Shoulder flexion showed poor agreement and camera-view dependence; 2D angles require application-specific validation.
facefit_limitations: Shoulder flexion is not shoulder-line tilt
Arm and trunk keypoints outside Face-Fit scope
